text:
ara: Quick alert from the int8 onboarding bench for orpheus-v1: small but reproducible drop on locales that mix Hebrew/Arabic and CJK. Looks tied to punctuation and ZERO-WIDTH chars.
tomo: Minimal repro please?
ara: Pasting trimmed case and tokenizer outputs:
```
Source: 

ב東京
FP16 tokens: ["\u05D1","\u00B7","\u6771","\u4EAC","\u30FB","\u200D"]
INT8 tokens: ["\u05D1","\u30FB","\u6771","\u4EAC","\u002D","\u200C"]
```
(tl;dr: U+200D vs U+200C and mid-dot vs hyphen flip; control bytes injected by some pipeline step)
leah: Huh. Did the int8 artifact build change the tokenizer binary or the normalization flags? We recently trimmed vocab for memory.
ara: Yes, int8 build used compacted vocab + our legacy runtime still uses an old ICU-based normalizer in hosted and a newer python normalizer in the lab.
tomo: That would explain mismatch: different normalizers map ZWJ/ZWSP differently around RTL/CJK boundaries. Quant changes alone shouldn't change input token ids but the trimmed vocab + serializer probably changed the mapping table ordering.
ci-bot: smoke-run orpheus-v1-int8 4945000020: bleu_base=19.2, bleu_int8=16.7, chrf_base=0.524, chrf_int8=0.489, regression_count=321, top-pattern="zwj-zwc-punct-shift"
leah: Short-term mitigations: (1) canonicalize ingress: NFKC + explicit mapping table for ZWJ/ZWSP/dash/dot; (2) add a check in build that tokenizer artifact for compact vocab has same mapping for control-range chars; (3) add unit fixtures mixing RTL+CJK with explicit ZWJ/ZWSP.
ara: I prototyped a tiny canonicalizer: s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s); s = s.replace('\u200D', '\u200C'); s = s.replace('\u00B7', '\u30FB'); s = s.replace('\u2014', '-'); and we log replaced counts to telemetry. Tokens line up locally.
tomo: Good. We should gate with a canary config tokenize.canonicalize_unicode=true and route 2% of int8 traffic. I'll schedule tonight. Also add assert in tokenizer tests: for each fixture assert token_ids_fp16 == token_ids_int8 when canonicalize flag true.
leah: Assign owners: tomo -> canary rollout, ara -> canonicalizer PR, leah -> test fixtures + build-verifier.
ara: If canary doesn't reduce regressions by >90% we'll open a follow-up to audit tokenizer serialization and compact-vocab ordering.
ci-bot: canary-plan created 4945000033: 2% routing, auto-collect BLEU/chrF and token-dump traces.
leah: thanks all, keep brief updates here.
